newsitem.title: USA: Hollinger closes public offering of notes.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger closes public offering of notes.

text.p: Hollinger International Inc said on Tuesday that it and its Hollinger International Publishing Inc subsidiary have closed their previously announced underwritten public offering of $260 million principal amount of 8-5/8 percent senior notes due March 15, 2005 ("Senior Notes").
Hollinger also said it closed the $290,000,000 principal amount of 9 1/4 percent senior subordinated notes due March 15, 2007 (the "Senior Subordinated Notes") issued by Hollinger Publishing.

Hollinger has guaranteed payment of the principal of, premium if any and interest on the Senior Notes on an unsecured senior basis, and on the Senior Subordinated Notes on an unsecured senior subordinated basis.

The Senior Notes, rated Ba3 by Moody's Investor Service, Inc. and BB+ by Standard & Poors, are priced at 99.5 percent of par. The Senior Subordinated Notes, rated B1 by Moody's Investor Service, Inc. and BB- by Standard & Poors, are priced at 99.358 percent of par.

The net proceeds of $523.3 million will be used to repay approximately $354.9 million of bank debt. The balance will be used to redeem certain outstanding preference shares of English subsidiaries held by third parties (at an aggregate redemption price of approximately $124.2 million) at their respective redemption dates in May and June 1997 and for general corporate purposes.
Hollinger publishes English-language newspapers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada and Israel.
